top3.title: Seated Stick Fighting
top3.venue: Wooden Shoe Books, 704 South St, Philadelphia, PA 19147
top3.why: Strange Fox Fighting Arts teaches a seated adaptation of bataireacht (Irish stick/shillelagh fighting) built specifically for people who can't stand at all or for long — disability justice framed as genuine self-defense instruction, not a token accommodation. Trans folks are prioritized to the front and welcome throughout; bring a cane if you have one, sticks are provided. Free, at Wooden Shoe Books, the anarchist bookstore that consistently runs this kind of accessible, community-first programming.

It's the opening night of the Stagecrafters' 97th season. Chestnut Hill; reachable via SEPTA's Chestnut Hill East or West Regional Rail lines.

top3.why: A 40th-anniversary screening of David Lynch's Blue Velvet — the film that codified Lynch's whole unsettling small-town-noir mode, with Kyle MacLachlan, Laura Dern, and Isabella Rossellini. PhilaMOCA's repertory programming is the right room for it. $13.20.

top3.title: Lady Sarkazym
top3.venue: City Winery, 990 Filbert St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
top3.why: Let's Build brings a curated set of poets — Lady Sarkazym joined by Lady Syren, Sam I Am, Jay Smoov, and E The Poet-Emcee — through single, resonant pieces on love, trust, healing, and self-worth, each followed by open conversation rather than a quick set change. It's City Winery's dinner-show polish applied to a genuinely community-built spoken-word night, not a commercial booking.
